chunks: And it is narrated from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: A man had dirhams owed to him by another man from the price of sheep that he had bought from him. Then the creditor came to the debtor demanding payment, so the debtor said to him: I will sell you these sheep for the dirhams that you have with me. So he agreed.
He عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that.

key_terms.أَبِيعُكَ: I sell to you; the debtor's offer of sale
key_terms.الطَّالِبُ: the creditor; the one seeking repayment
key_terms.الْمَطْلُوبُ: the debtor; the one from whom payment is sought
key_terms.ثَمَنِ: price; the purchase value giving rise to the debt
key_terms.غَنَمٍ: sheep; the commodity involved in both the original and subsequent sale
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِذَلِكَ: there is no harm in that; indicating legal permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islamic law to settle a debt by selling goods to the creditor for the amount owed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling permitting a debtor to sell goods to his creditor in exchange for the debt already owed. It indicates the permissibility of settling a financial obligation through a mutually agreed sale using the existing debt amount.
